creature.name: Agadaz

mid.name: Risk Aura
entries: 30 feet. A feeling of recklessness surrounds a gambling devil. When a non-fiend creature enters the aura or begins its turn in the aura, it must attempt a DC 21 Will save.

mid.name: Critical Success
entries: The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Risk Aura for 24 hours.

mid.name: Success
entries: The creature is unaffected.

mid.name: Failure
entries: The next time the creature rolls a d20, it must roll twice. If either roll is a natural 20, the creature uses that result; otherwise, it must take the lower of the two results.

mid.name: Critical Failure
entries: As failure, but applies to all of the creature's d20 rolls as long as it remains in the aura.

mid.name: Double Down
mid.trigger: The agadaz attempts a Strike, saving throw, or skill check
entries: The agadaz takes a –2 status penalty to the roll, then gains a +2 status bonus to the next Strike, saving throw, or skill check they attempt before the end of their turn, or before the end of their next turn if they used Double Down during another creature's turn.

mid.name: Produce Gold Coins
entries: The agadaz creates up to 5 gp in their hand. At any one time, an agadaz can possess no more than 20 gp created in this way; coins created in excess of this value vanish. A coin created in this way vanishes automatically 1 hour after leaving the devil's possession.

entries: The spark of the soul used to create a masque mannequin is infused into its mask. _aon.markdown:
Masque mannequins are a type of soulbound construct animated by a fragment of a once-living soul infused into an eerie, nearly featureless mask that's then affixed to a mannequin or dressmaker's dummy. Though similar in process to the creation of a soulbound doll or mannequin, creating a masque mannequin requires conducting ritualistic murder and extracting a soul shard during an unwilling victim's death, and only the vilest of crafters would consider attempting such a deed. Masque mannequins are popular among [Norgorberites](/Deities.aspx?ID=289), especially devotees of Father Skinsaw, as well as [Kuthites](/Deities.aspx?ID=296) who take pride in drawing out the ritual to gain the largest possible fragment of the soul. **[Recall Knowledge - Construct](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)): DC 36 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 34 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 31 [Masque Mannequin](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3745) **Source** [Pathfinder #205: Singer, Stalker, Skinsaw Man](/Sources.aspx?ID=246) pg. 87 **Perception** +26; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** one spoken in life (typically [Common](/Languages.aspx?ID=155); can't speak any language) **Skills** [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) +29, [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +29, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +29 **Str** +8 **Dex** +6 **Con** +5 **Int** -2 **Wis** +3 **Cha** +0 **Soul Mask** The spark of the soul used to create a masque mannequin is infused into its mask. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) for 1 round as its body grows more wooden.
**Failure** The creature is [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=87) for the next 24 hours, but instead of turning to stone, it turns into a wooden mannequin. It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns.

Malevolent Mindsets Masque mannequins, even those crafted from virtuous individuals, tend to have a sadistic sense of malice. If left to their own devices, a masque mannequin enjoys playing cat and mouse games with their chosen victims by freezing and unfreezing in areas with mundane mannequins, slowly driving their unfortunate playthings to paranoia before going for the kill.

creature.name: Shanty Chanter

mid.name: Seasong
entries: A shanty chanter aboard a vessel that uses wind propulsion can use this exploration activity to call up lightly buffeting winds. The chanter can Sustain this effect for up to 8 hours, during which the vessel they're on benefits from the propulsion in the desired direction. Seasong is overwhelmed and negated by powerful storms.

mid.name: Shanty Call
entries: The shanty chanter begins to sing a catchy sea shanty and selects up to 10 allies within 60 feet who can hear the shanty chanter to potentially join in. Selected allies feel an urge to join but aren't required to—a targeted ally can join as a Reaction. A shanty chanter can Sustain Shanty Call as a Reaction at the start of their turn for up to 1 minute. While sustained, the shanty chanter and all allies who joined the shanty when they began to sing become quickened and can use the extra action to Climb, Force Open, Reposition, Shove, Strike, or Swim. When the shanty chanter ceases to Sustain Shanty Call, they and all allies who were affected become fatigued for 1 minute.

_aon.markdown:
<title level="1" pfs="">[Shanty Chanter](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3746)</title>

<row gap="medium">

<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

Shanty chanters are known to dwell along the coasts of Garund or the eastern isles of the Shackles, living on small islands or cliffsides but rarely venturing too far inland. These capricious fey have humanoid torsos and seagull heads, wings, and feet, and they stand about 5 feet tall. Consummate performers, shanty chanters adore music, especially the sea shanties sung by ships' crews. The songs from these fey's aeries can be heard from miles away over the open sea. While some sailors claim these songs intentionally lure mortals to drown, most shanty chanters aren't outright malevolent and would be more inclined to investigate a foundering ship than to slaughter those aboard, even if they do relieve such a vessel of its valuables.

 Shanty chanters have a particular affinity for pirate ships, and a captain who wins an alliance with an aerie of shanty chanters is considered blessed with good luck. Of course, this attention can be a double-edged sword. If a captain fails to appease the ship's allied shanty chanters (generally by giving them a fair share of the plunder gained while they're on board), the affronted fey afflicts the captain with a mariner's curse before departing for more prosperous shores.

<aside>
<title level="2" noclass="true" icon="/images/Icons/Sidebar_2_AdditionalLore.png">Chanter Vanity</title>

Shanty chanters are quite vain, adorning themselves in jewelry obtained in the raids of their allied ships or taken in raids of their own. They appreciate flattery toward both their physical appearances and musical talents, and they view this type of bribe to be as valuable as material goods. Conversely, the surest way to gain a shanty chanter's enmity is to insult their singing, and only the deeply unwise would dare such a thing.
</aside>

mid.name: Memento Vulnerability
entries: Waxen effigies retain an attachment to objects they had a strong tie to in life. A character who holds such a memento in a hand can use it to alter the effects of Demoralize. Doing so adds the manipulate trait to Demoralize. _aon.markdown:
The undead ooze known as a waxen effigy forms under a specific set of circumstances, making such creatures quite rare. Most waxen effigies arise from botched rituals intended to migrate a powerful sapient creature's soul into a body made of wax, whether in a bid for immortality or a method of imprisonment or sacrifice. The death—especially a traumatic death—of a sapient creature in close proximity to a wax figure or while attempting to craft a construct out of wax might also result in a waxen effigy. A waxen effigy looks like a partially melted wax version of who it appeared as in life. They retain little of their former personality but recall a jumble of memories from their mortal existence that serves only to anger them. They often cling to objects that were important to them in life, such as a spouse's wedding band or a tool from a favorite hobby. Displaying such an object to a waxen effigy transfixes their attention, though they often lash out if the object is taken away before they can be laid to rest. **[Recall Knowledge - Ooze](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)): DC 43 **[Recall Knowledge - Undead](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)** ([Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46)): DC 43 **[Unspecific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 41 **[Specific Lore](/Rules.aspx?ID=563)**: DC 38 [Waxen Effigy](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3747) **Source** [Pathfinder #205: Singer, Stalker, Skinsaw Man](/Sources.aspx?ID=246) pg. 89 **Perception** +29; [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=59) **Languages** [Necril](/Languages.aspx?ID=20); one language known in life (can't speak any language) **Skills** [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) +35, [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=48) +32 **Str** +9 **Dex** +4 **Con** +7 **Int** -1 **Wis** +5 **Cha** +0 --- **AC** 38 **Fort** +31 **Ref** +24 **Will** +27 **HP** 415 ([void healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=83)) **Immunities** [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=571) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=578), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) **Weaknesses** [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) 15 **Memento Vulnerability** Waxen effigies retain an attachment to objects they had a strong tie to in life. A character who holds such a memento in a hand can use it to alter the effects of [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=2395). Doing so adds the [manipulate](/Actions.aspx?ID=2229) trait to Demoralize. If the attempt to Demoralize the waxen effigy is successful, it becomes [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) (slowed 2 on a critical success) for 1 round rather than becoming [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76). ### Waxen Effigy

The undead ooze known as a waxen effigy forms under a specific set of circumstances, making such creatures quite rare. Most waxen effigies arise from botched rituals intended to migrate a powerful sapient creature's soul into a body made of wax, whether in a bid for immortality or a method of imprisonment or sacrifice. The death—especially a traumatic death—of a sapient creature in close proximity to a wax figure or while attempting to craft a construct out of wax might also result in a waxen effigy.

A waxen effigy looks like a partially melted wax version of who it appeared as in life. They retain little of their former personality but recall a jumble of memories from their mortal existence that serves only to anger them. They often cling to objects that were important to them in life, such as a spouse's wedding band or a tool from a favorite hobby. Displaying such an object to a waxen effigy transfixes their attention, though they often lash out if the object is taken away before they can be laid to rest.
